summary: Iteration 2 testing of new features (team self-registration, image upload via Emergent Object Storage, age categories, role-scoped permissions). Backend: 44/44 pytest tests pass = 24 regression (auth, teams, players, matches, standings, scorers, inventory, bookings) + 20 new (categories endpoint, register-team, /auth/me team_id, team-vs-team RBAC on teams & players, inventory still admin-only, /upload auth+mime+size, /api/files public serving). Image upload to Emergent Object Storage works end-to-end (uploaded 1x1 PNG, retrieved via public /api/files/... URL with correct content-type, byte-for-byte identical). Frontend: /registro-equipo loads, categories dropdown populated correctly with [Sub-8, Sub-10, Sub-12, Sub-14, Sub-16, Sub-18], team registration redirects to /mi-equipo, MyTeam page renders team info, Edit Team modal includes CategorySelect + ImageUpload, AdminTeams/AdminPlayers/AdminInventario all use CategorySelect & ImageUpload widgets, admin login redirects to /admin, anonymous /mi-equipo redirects to /login (ProtectedRoute working), no page-level JS errors.

minor.issue: When team manager edits their own player, the body still requires team_id in payload (PlayerIn). If a malicious team passes their own team_id but tries to move another team's player, the check at line 515 catches it (existing.team_id != user.team_id), but the same endpoint will 403 if a team manager tries to *change* team_id for their own player to something else. Acceptable by design but worth documenting.
Every request hits Mongo for record lookup AND a remote GET to the object-storage endpoint - no caching or Cache-Control headers. On a public images page this could be slow / costly.
5MB limit applied AFTER reading entire body into memory. Large files still consume memory before being rejected. Consider streaming or reading chunked.
If db.users insert fails after db.teams insert succeeds (e.g., duplicate index race), the team document is orphaned with no rollback.

integration_issues.issue: When value starts with /api/, preview src is built using API_BASE.replace(/\/api$/, '') from lib/api. If REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL ends with /api the slice works; otherwise prefix may be doubled. Currently same-origin so /api/files/... resolves through ingress and works.

issues: Helper text below logo upload says 'Para subir imagen necesitas iniciar sesión primero' which is correct (upload requires auth) but somewhat confusing on a registration page - users can only attach a logo AFTER registering. Consider hiding the ImageUpload until after registration or making it optional with clearer copy.

action_items: Optional: add Cache-Control headers to /api/files/{path} responses for public images.
Optional: clarify or hide logo upload on /registro-equipo (upload requires existing auth; users can add logo after first login from /mi-equipo).
Optional: roll back team insert if user insert fails in /auth/register-team.
Carry-over from iter1 (still relevant): server.py is now 875 lines (>700 threshold) - split into routers (auth/teams/players/matches/inventory/bookings/uploads).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py grew from 691 to 875 lines after adding storage + new endpoints. Past the 700-line threshold; modularize into routers/services.

Object storage init keeps a module-level _storage_key cache; first request after server start triggers init lazily AND startup also calls init_storage(). On 403 the code refreshes once but propagates raise_for_status() - missing storage will surface as 5xx to the user.
MIME whitelist hard-codes only 5 extensions but /api/upload accepts file.content_type from client. Consider validating content_type independently.

/api/files/{path:path} is intentionally unauthenticated. Path is whitelisted by the db.files lookup so direct enumeration of arbitrary storage paths is blocked - good. However, anyone with the URL can fetch it forever; consider TTL signed URLs for sensitive uploads later.
register-team does NOT check/enforce that manager_user_id is unique; a single user can manage one team because the unique index is on email, but team.manager_user_id has no index/uniqueness.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on flows tested (registration redirect, MyTeam render, CategorySelect & ImageUpload presence on all admin pages, RBAC redirects)

Run both: `pytest /app/backend/tests/ -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/results.xml`. Both pass with admin creds from /app/memory/test_credentials.md. New routes: /registro-equipo (TeamRegister), /mi-equipo (MyTeam protected by role=team). Key data-testids: tr-manager, tr-email, tr-password, tr-team-name, tr-category, tr-coach, tr-city, tr-submit, my-team-page, edit-team-btn, save-team-btn, add-player-btn, save-player-btn, player-name-input, player-jersey-input, category-select, *-image-upload, *-image-upload-btn, *-image-upload-input. ImageUpload posts multipart to /api/upload (auth required), returns {url: '/api/files/...'} which can drop into via same-origin ingress proxy. Object storage uses EMERGENT_LLM_KEY from backend/.env.
